title: Conservation and Science
copy: Object Treatment. In 2025, the Conservation and Science team treated 1,116 artworks, care that ranged from light cleaning to multi-year restorations. For this monumental 19th-century punch bowl, objects conservator Haddon Dine spent two years removing discolored restorations, reassembling old breaks, and filling major losses, readying the work to debut in the new Eloise W. Martin Galleries of Applied Arts of Europe. Intersections in an Art Museum. Explore this toolkit designed for museum professionals, students, and anyone interested in learning about the interdisciplinary work of an art museum. Conservation and Science at the Art Institute of Chicago. Responsible for the treatment, research, and long-term preservation of more than 300,000 works of art in the Art Institute’s collections, the Department of Conservation and Science is integral to the museum’s mission to protect the world’s artistic and cultural legacy for future generations. Every artwork in the Art Institute’s collections—whether it’s on view in the galleries, maintained in storage, or traveling the globe—comes under the care of the Conservation and Science team. This group of dedicated experts uses their specialized knowledge and advanced skills to ensure that each object is studied, conserved, and shared with our audiences for generations to come. Explore this department’s wide-ranging expertise and projects, from conservation treatments to research discoveries and more. Recent Publications. Peruse some of the many papers the conservation and science team has published. Publication. Conservators and scientists regularly contribute articles to peer-reviewed journals and essays to exhibition and collection catalogues. Recently new findings about the materials used by ancient Egyptian artists were published in the new, freely accessible digital catalogue about the Art Institute’s collection of ancient Egyptian art—the museum's first diving into this important collection. Art + Science Educator Resource. This educator resource offers guidance and support for dialogue and collaboration between art and science teachers at the middle school level. Center for Scientific Studies in the Arts. Discover the collaborative research initiative combining the resources of Northwestern University and the Art Institute. Art + Science Videos and Curricula. These videos and their accompanying lesson plans explore science concepts and STEAM careers in museum conservation. Research. Research is continually underway—whether it winds up in a published article, is passed on to an institution where we’re loaning our work, or added to an object file to help us care for a work for decades to come. Currently research is being done to learn more about the painting materials used in Ethiopian artworks, including this 17th-century manuscript depicting the “Miracles of Mary.”
